subject: Decision Making
title: Voting Systems as Games
description: A quick, practical guide to Voting Systems as Games.

hook.text: Arrow's impossibility theorem proves no voting system can satisfy all fairness criteria at once.

buildup.text: First-past-the-post forces tactical voting. Third-party voters help their least-preferred candidate win.

discovery.text: Ranked choice, approval voting, and proportional systems each fix some problems but create new ones.

twist.text: Strategic voting is rational. If your candidate cannot win, switching to your second choice is smart game theory.

climax.text: Every voting system is a game with rules that shape outcomes. Change the rules and the winners change too.

punchline.text: No perfect voting system exists. The rules shape who wins. Math proved this.

quiz.question: What does Arrow's impossibility theorem prove?
options: No voting system can satisfy all fairness criteria simultaneously
